pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
<!--- Describe the change below, including rationale and design decisions -->
Fixes #66341

- The `join_path` method in `powershell.py` didn't preserve the leading double backslashes in UNC paths. A fix was added.
- A test was added for `join_path` that checks for correctness with a UNC path.

Sounds great to me! I originally looked at os.path support and saw it does Windows when running on Windows so I thought it wouldn't be doable on the controller code, but now seeing that it's aliased on Windows to ntpath I think?

I'll take a look at this again soon.

> but now seeing that it's aliased on Windows to ntpath I think?

Yep when running on Windows, `os.path` is just an alias for `ntpath`. This way we don't have to do any of the logic itself just use the tried and tested Python library for Windows paths :)

This turned out to be a little trickier than expected. 

First, `ntpath.join()` doesn't normalize the path on its own, so also needed `ntpath.normpath()` to resolve duplicated separators and converting `/` to `\`. 

Second issue is that `.join()` treats any path component beginning with a separator is an absolute path, and so it ignores all other non-drive components that came before it and begins from that component adding them to the drive. 

This results in these test components:
```['\\\\host\\share\\dir1\\\\dir2\\', '\\dir3/dir4', 'dir5', 'dir6\\']```
Being joined into this path:
```\\host\share\dir3\dir4\dir5\dir6```
(because the `dir3` component begins with `\`).

While this is probably technically correct behavior, it's unexpected and is not what the previous function did, so I opted to replicate the previous output so as not to break things that might have been relying on that. 

This was accomplished by `strip`ing separators from each component except the first.

If that's not the right call, let me know.

I think this one should actually be considered a bug. 

As far as I was able to tell, the problem was not in the `fetch` action itself. [`fetch` calls the current shell's `join_path` method](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/85f36a3a42c8148decf20cef8ef62729649682f1/lib/ansible/plugins/action/fetch.py#L71), and it's [the one in `powershell.py`](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/85f36a3a42c8148decf20cef8ef62729649682f1/lib/ansible/plugins/shell/powershell.py#L95) that ends up stripping off the slashes in the beginning.

Unfortunately with the method used, you wouldn't be able to work around it by adding any additional slashes to the beginning; they would all get removed.

I've added a small PR that seems to fix this, and a test for UNC paths that will hopefully catch it if it comes up again.

review_comments:
I don't necessarily see this behaviour, for example

```
import ntpath

ntpath.join("\\\\server\\share", "\\abc\\def\\", "\\ghi\\jkl\\", "mno\\pqr", "stu") == "\\\\server\\share\\ghi\\jkl\\mno\\pqr\\stu"
```

Am I misunderstanding what the stripping is for?

@jborean93 

> ```ntpath.join("\\\\server\\share", "\\abc\\def\\", "\\ghi\\jkl\\", "mno\\pqr", "stu") == "\\\\server\\share\\ghi\\jkl\\mno\\pqr\\stu"```

Your resulting path is missing `\\abc\\def` because it was superseded by `\\ghi\\jkl\\`. If `stu` were `\\stu`, then the result would be:

```\\\\server\\share\\stu```

It's "correct" in the sense that if your working directory is `C:\Users\jborean` and you ask to open the file `\Windows\WindowsUpdate.log`, the behavior you see is that it is opened (it combined the absolute-but-not-fully-qualified path with the current drive).

It's just not typically what we'd use `join_path` for and the previous version of it split on separators and rejoined them so it had no concept of this and would have included all components. It was actually the test I added that caught this as I hadn't realized it myself when I was playing with `ntpath` directly.

I went with reproducing the previous function's output so as not to break things that were (probably inadvertently) relying on it, but let me know if you think
Ahh ok that makes sense, was on auto pilot when I was testing it out. Thanks for clarifying.
